principle: The user is not the system maintenance operator. A user correction, systemic defect, drift, propagation gap, regression, lifecycle ambiguity, maintainability issue, repeated owner failure, premature solution canonicalization, or global-audit signal starts a maintenance process; it is not a direct implementation order. The maintenance writer must classify the signal, inspect the affected system, decide what must be learned or changed, and only then execute the smallest evidence-backed change.

meta_maintenance_outline.purpose: Default governance path for non-trivial systemic maintenance. It prevents symptom-driven patching, blind obedience to proposed fixes, prompt-only papering-over, cross-subsystem drift, and unbounded architecture growth.

activation.lightweight_depth: Local, reversible, low-coupling defects still pass through the same classifications, but external scouting and broad owner sweeps may be NOT_REQUIRED_WITH_REASON.

mandatory_questions: What exact user goal/constraint/counterexample was revealed, separate from the proposed mechanism?
What is the root-cause layer: account/prompt instruction, repository policy, runtime, schema, test/eval, owner binding, product capability, evidence, or propagation?
What other active surfaces can contradict or bypass this fix?
What relevant prior incidents, accepted rules, user corrections, and current external practices should be learned before choosing a fix?
What credible alternative includes deletion/simplification/no-change rather than only adding another layer?
Does this require changing GPT/account/startup instructions, or would that merely mask a runtime/schema/test defect?
Will child owners/subsystems inherit the invariant automatically, or are there stale overrides/shadow copies?
What does the change add to startup context, tool calls, latency, authority surfaces, migration burden, and maintenance coupling?
What old mechanism is superseded and must be removed/demoted?
What negative/held-out/cross-surface evidence could falsify the accepted fix?
What is the exact assurance ceiling and what remains unknown?

user_feedback_assimilation.principle: Material user corrections are first-class reliability/eval evidence, not direct architecture commands and not disposable chat feedback.
user_feedback_assimilation.external_account_instruction_action_if_r: Stabilize repository semantics first, persist the exact minimal account-level delta, then ask the user once because repository writes cannot mutate ChatGPT account instructions.

change_instruction_when: behavior must activate before repository authority can be loaded
a durable user-facing product instruction cannot be enforced by runtime alone
do_not_change_instruction_when: runtime/schema/test can mechanically enforce the invariant
the proposed instruction would duplicate repository authority
the change only makes a stale lower-level implementation appear compliant
instruction_surface_review.anti_bloat_rule: Prefer a short routing/activation instruction that delegates to current repository authority over copying maintenance doctrine into Custom Instructions.

learning_evolution_review.principle: Learning is a required decision point, not mandatory browsing theater. Non-trivial/systemic maintenance must explicitly decide SCOUT_REQUIRED or NOT_REQUIRED_WITH_REASON.
preferred_inputs: current internal incidents and user corrections
current first-party OpenAI documentation for OpenAI behavior
original engineering documentation/repos for studied systems

closure_claim_limits.rule: A completed maintenance pass means the scoped process closed with bounded evidence; it never means the entire evolving system is globally flawless.

authority_surface_admission_gate.anti_pattern: User reports a symptom -> create another policy/prompt/role without architecture classification.
authority_surface_admission_gate.failed_admission_behavior: Consolidate into the existing authority or implement the missing executable/test mechanism; do not accumulate parallel documentation.

reliability_guard.principle: Repeated material failure is a system reliability signal. A single material correction may already trigger a system-impact review when it exposes a plausible shared failure class.
incident_triggers: same defect class materially recurs after an accepted fix
the user repeatedly has to restate the same durable requirement
a single material user correction exposes a plausible shared control-plane failure class
the user repeatedly has to correct the system for treating the user's suggested mechanism or analogy as canonical architecture
a mandatory gate is repeatedly bypassed or falsely reported
the owner repeatedly executes from stale rules, stale state, or stale artifacts
CI, eval, or product evidence shows a regression in a core owner responsibility

system_audit_strategy.principle: Audit depth is selected by risk and change impact. Do not run every owner business pipeline on every maintenance turn; do not use a light targeted check when a cross-cutting change makes wider uncertainty material.

CORE_ALWAYS.activation: every control-plane CI run and every material maintenance closure

checks: affected owner adapters or capability pointers

OWNER_SENTINEL_ROTATION.activation: owner-related maintenance or active maintenance turns where additional confidence is useful without a full sweep
checks: no business execution or lease takeover
relevant owner-specific regressions without stealing owner leases

SYNTHETIC_FAULT_INJECTION.activation: explicit global audit, systemic incident, or high-risk architecture/reliability boundary where negative evidence is needed
checks: stale registry tries to override owner authority
new-chat takeover fails to change lease
external reference promoted to authority by presence
declared executor treated as current-session proof
meta-maintenance outline omitted after systemic correction
hard-coded stale methodology receipt semantics survive contract upgrade
SYNTHETIC_FAULT_INJECTION.safety: Use deterministic fixtures or non-production experiments by default.

decision_rules: Routine low-risk changes run CORE_ALWAYS + IMPACT_SCOPED.
A change to protocol, authority, registry, startup/discovery, storage/artifact governance, methodology contract, execution contract, or system-maintenance method escalates to FULL_CONTROL_PLANE.
Explicit deep audit, systemic incident, or user challenge to maintenance completeness activates the full meta-maintenance outline and SYNTHETIC_FAULT_INJECTION.
Full owner business pipelines are not a default audit primitive.
A full control-plane sweep may read all owner metadata/pointers but must not steal active owner leases or mutate business truth.
Unknown-unknown coverage comes from negative scenarios, contradiction scans, stale/dangling reference checks and boundary tests, not from an unbounded checklist.
Efficiency is part of correctness: a repair that materially increases steady-state context/tool/latency cost without proportional reliability value fails design review.

preferred_locations: audit or research artifact when detail is substantial
Git commit history for file-level change history
